title: GPT-5 Prompt Anatomy — OpenAI's six-part role-to-stop-condition template
summary: A worked example of OpenAI's GPT-5 prompting structure: Role, Task, Context, Reasoning, Output format and Stop conditions, shown on a 'find three under-the-radar hikes near San Francisco' prompt. The useful bits are the explicit self-vetting step and a stop condition that defines when the answer is done.
takeaways: Split prompts into role, task, context, reasoning, output format and stop condition blocks.
Ask the model to internally verify facts against named sources before answering.
Define a concrete completion test so the model knows when to stop.

title: Claude Code Team Tips — Boris Cherny's 10 habits for parallel, plan-first agent work
summary: Boris Cherny's thread of tips from the Claude Code team: 3-5 git worktrees with parallel sessions, plan mode for every complex task, a CLAUDE.md you update after each correction, skills committed to git, Slack MCP bug fixing, subagents, a BigQuery skill for analytics and learning output styles. It ends with a ready-to-paste CLAUDE.md workflow template (plan, subagents, lessons file, verify before done).
takeaways: Run 3-5 worktrees each with its own Claude session; name them and alias them for fast switching.
Start complex work in plan mode and re-plan when things drift instead of pushing on.
End every correction with 'update your CLAUDE.md so you don't make that mistake again'.
Turn anything done daily into a skill or slash command, such as /techdebt, and commit it.

title: Consulting-Grade Prompt Pack — 12 Claude prompts for TAM, SWOT, pricing and GTM
summary: Twelve fill-in-the-blank prompts that cast Claude as a McKinsey, Bain or Goldman analyst: TAM/SAM/SOM sizing, competitive landscape, personas, trend analysis, SWOT plus Porter's Five Forces, pricing, go-to-market, journey mapping, unit economics, risk scenarios, market entry and a master synthesis prompt. A handy scaffold for a founder's first-pass strategy doc; the 'replaces $5,000 consultants' framing is hype, and the outputs still need real data.
takeaways: Each prompt pairs a senior persona with an explicit deliverable list and format, a reusable pattern.
Use the master synthesis prompt last to fold the earlier analyses into one recommendation.
Treat outputs as structured hypotheses; plug in real market data before trusting the numbers.

title: CLAUDE.md Workflow Template — plan mode, subagents and a lessons loop
summary: The CLAUDE.md template attributed to Boris Cherny's workflow: plan mode for any task of 3+ steps, liberal subagent use, a tasks/lessons.md file updated after every correction, verification before marking done, 'demand elegance', and autonomous bug fixing. The caption adds that he runs 10-15 Claude sessions in parallel across terminal and web; the same template also closes the fuller tips thread in this batch.
takeaways: Write the plan to tasks/todo.md with checkable items and log corrections to tasks/lessons.md.
Never mark a task done without proving it works, for example by diffing behavior against main.
Use subagents to keep the main context window clean.

title: ChatGPT Prompt Stack — 7 role and memory prompts fronting an AI-agency pitch
summary: Seven generic ChatGPT prompts (role architecture, brain upload, outcome simulator, feedback loop, step-gated chain, session checkpoints, three-way refiner) used as the hook for a 'Remote Triaging' AI-automation agency pitch built on Apollo.io, Perplexity, Make.com, Unipile and Vapi. Mostly lead-gen for a DM funnel; the prompts are basic.
takeaways: The session-checkpoint and ask-me-three-questions prompts are the only reusable ideas.
The agency stack is Apollo for leads, Perplexity for enrichment, Make for glue, Unipile for outreach and Vapi for calls.

title: Ad Deconstruction with GPT-4o — reverse-engineer a winning ad, regenerate for your brand
summary: A three-step workflow: upload a competitor ad to ChatGPT, have it analyze psychology, imagery, typography, color and composition through Cialdini, Rory Sutherland and William Leach personas, then map those tactics to your brand and generate a new image ad with your product shot. Shown on a serum ad remade for a cleanser brand.
takeaways: Copy the reasoning behind an ad rather than the ad itself.
Ask for a component-by-component breakdown before asking for adaptation.
Attach your own product photos so the generated ad stays on-brand.

title: Government Contract Brokering Prompts — ChatGPT playbook for subcontracting middlemen
summary: Six ChatGPT prompts for finding government contract platforms, decoding RFPs, writing proposals as a coordinator, sourcing subcontractors, a compliance checklist and a multi-contract system. It is engagement bait for a '700+ AI tools' DM giveaway, and the zero-cost middleman pitch glosses over real registration and compliance work.
takeaways: The contract-analyzer prompt, which turns an RFP into plain English plus requirements, is the one worth keeping.
Verify registration steps against official procurement sites, not model output.

title: Mentor-Style GitHub Repos — five repos for terminal, patterns, testing and architecture
summary: Five learning repos: jlevy/the-art-of-command-line for real terminal fluency, kilimchoi/engineering-blogs for company engineering write-ups, RefactoringGuru/design-patterns-typescript for GoF patterns with real-world examples, abhivaikar/howtheytest for how companies test, and gothinkster/realworld, the same Medium clone across many frontends and backends.
takeaways: RealWorld lets you compare one app spec implemented across many frameworks.
How They Test now lives at abhivaikar.github.io/howtheytest.
The Art of Command Line is a fast way to level up everyday shell use.

title: VectorBT Grid Search — mmap data, joblib batching and vectorized backtests
summary: A speed recipe for strategy grid searches with VectorBT: load OHLCV via numpy memmap (mmap_mode='r', copy=False) to avoid RAM blowups, fan thousands of backtests across cores with joblib Parallel, batch tasks in groups of 1,000, and run Portfolio.from_signals with fees and slippage as Numba-compiled matrix ops. Illustrated with a BTC moving-average crossover return surface.
takeaways: Use np.load(..., mmap_mode='r') and DataFrame(copy=False) to backtest many tickers without RAM spikes.
Batch joblib tasks to keep all cores saturated and cut process overhead.
Always pass fees and slippage into Portfolio.from_signals so grid winners are not fee artifacts.

title: ASI-Evolve — open-source agent loop that autonomously designs AI architectures
summary: ASI-Evolve, from Shanghai Jiao Tong University and Shanghai Innovation Institute, is an open-source agentic framework that automates AI research in a learn-design-experiment-analyze loop across data, architecture and learning algorithms. The paper reports 105 autonomously discovered architectures, with the best beating DeltaNet. The video also touches on China's AGI framing in its five-year plan.
takeaways: A closed learn-design-experiment-analyze loop can search data, architecture and optimizer choices together.
Read the paper's DeltaNet comparison before believing the 'tripled human gains' claim.
Open code means you can try the loop on your own small-model experiments.

title: Open-Source SaaS Replacements — 10 repos from yt-dlp and Ollama to n8n and Penpot
summary: A list of free self-hostable alternatives to paid tools: yt-dlp, Ollama for local models, Fooocus for image generation, Whisper for transcription, Plausible Analytics, AppFlowy for Notion, Penpot for Figma, n8n for Zapier, Cal.com or its MIT fork Cal.diy for Calendly, and Bitwarden for 1Password. Well-known picks with inflated pricing comparisons, but a solid checklist.
takeaways: Penpot and AppFlowy are the self-hosted answers to Figma and Notion seats.
n8n self-hosted removes per-task automation pricing.
Cal.diy is an MIT-only fork of Cal.com with the enterprise code removed.

title: Claude Code on Open Models — proxy routing to OpenRouter or Kimi K2.6
summary: Pitches an unnamed GitHub tool, around 25k stars, that sits in front of Claude Code and routes its requests to open-source models via OpenRouter or a Kimi API key, with model switching through /model. The video never names the repo, and the 'Claude free forever' line means Claude Code's interface running on other models, not Claude itself.
takeaways: Claude Code can be pointed at other models through an Anthropic-compatible proxy.
Expect quality differences; '90% of the performance' is the creator's claim.

title: Graphify — turn a repo into a knowledge graph to cut Claude Code tokens
summary: Graphify is a free open-source tool that converts a repository, or a folder of markdown and unstructured notes, into a knowledge graph that Claude Code or other coding agents query as a map. Answers come from the graph instead of re-reading files, so codebase questions use far fewer tokens: a kind of lightweight RAG.
takeaways: Build the graph once per repo and have the agent query it before opening raw files.
It also works on markdown-only repos as a lightweight retrieval layer.
